items.title: Israeli police bar patriarch from Holy Sepulchre on Palm Sunday

featured_image.name: Israeli police block Catholic cardinal from Holy Sepulchre on Palm ...

items.description:
Israeli police on Sunday barred Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa, the Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem, from entering the Church of the Holy Sepulchre to celebrate Palm Sunday Mass, marking what church leaders called the first time in centuries that the ceremony could not be held at one of Christianity's holiest sites. The incident drew swift condemnation from world leaders, the Vatican, and even the U.S. ambassador to Israel.

According to the Associated Press, Pizzaballa and Father Francesco Ielpo, the custodian of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, were walking privately toward the church — without any procession or ceremony — when Israeli police stopped them and forced them to turn back. Israeli police said they had informed the church on Saturday that no Mass would be permitted, citing safety concerns tied to the ongoing war with Iran, the inability of emergency vehicles to navigate the Old City's narrow streets, and insufficient bomb shelters.[1][2]

items.title: Iran warns U.S. ground troops would be 'set on fire' as diplomats push for talks

featured_image.name: Iran warns U.S. ground invasion would see troops “set on fire,”  state media reports

items.description:
As the U.S. war with Iran enters its fifth week, the Trump administration is weighing increasingly aggressive options that could put American boots on the ground in Iran, including operations to seize the country's enriched uranium stockpile and its critical oil export hub on Kharg Island.

Iran's parliament speaker warned the United States on Sunday against a ground invasion, threatening to escalate attacks on American allies, according to CBS News. The warning came as foreign ministers from Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Egypt convened in Pakistan to push for a diplomatic end to the conflict, even as fresh airstrikes hit Tehran over the weekend.[1][2][3]

items.title: Brent crude tops $116 as Houthi attack widens Middle East conflict

featured_image.name: Strait of Hormuz crisis explained: What it means for global shipping

items.description:
Yemen's Houthi rebels launched their first missile attack on Israel since the start of the U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran, sending oil prices sharply higher and raising fears that a second critical shipping chokepoint could be closed off to global trade.

The Iranian-backed group fired a barrage of ballistic missiles at what it described as "sensitive Israeli military sites" in southern Israel on Saturday, triggering sirens around Beersheba and near Israel's primary nuclear research facility. The Israeli military said it successfully intercepted one missile, and no injuries were reported. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree declared the strikes would continue until "the aggression against all resistance fronts" ends.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Iran warns against ground invasion as diplomats meet in Pakistan

featured_image.name: Pakistan maintains 'delicate balancing act' as it hosts Iran talks

items.description:
Foreign ministers from Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Egypt gathered in Islamabad on Sunday for a two-day summit aimed at charting a path toward ending the month-long war between the United States, Israel, and Iran, even as fighting continued and Tehran publicly rejected the terms on offer. Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar is leading the talks, which officials have described as the most coordinated regional diplomatic effort since the conflict began on February 28.[1][2][3]

Neither the United States, Iran, nor Israel is participating in the meetings. Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said the goal was to open "direct dialogue" between Washington and Tehran, which have so far communicated only through intermediaries. Turkey's Hakan Fidan and Saudi Arabia's Prince Faisal bin Farhan rounded out the gathering, which Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif set up after holding what he called "extensive discussions" with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Saturday.[3][4][5]
